_meta.indication: LOKELMA is a potassium binder indicated for the treatment of hyperkalemia in adults. It should not be used as an emergency treatment for life-threatening hyperkalemia because of its delayed onset of action.
_meta.receipt_date: November 22, 2017 (resubmission constituting complete response to the March 16, 2017 action letter; original NDA received May 26, 2015).

pivotal_trials.design: Two-part, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial with a 48-hour acute phase and a 12-day subacute (maintenance) phase; patients randomized to placebo or ZS 1.25 g, 2.5 g, 5 g, or 10 g.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with mild to moderate hyperkalemia (5 to 6.5 mEq/L, mean potassium 5.3 mEq/L).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Acute phase: difference in the exponential rate of change in serum potassium during the initial 48 hours between placebo and LOKELMA.
pivotal_trials.n: Acute phase randomized: placebo 158, ZS 1.25 g 154, ZS 2.5 g 141, ZS 5 g 157, ZS 10 g 143.
pivotal_trials.result: Acute phase primary endpoint met: exponential rate of change vs placebo p=0.0009 (2.5 g), p<0.0001 (5 g), p<0.0001 (10 g); mean serum potassium change at 48 h -0.7 mEq/L for 10 g TID vs -0.2 mEq/L placebo. Maintenance/subacute phase met at 5 and 10 g doses (p<0.01 and p<0.001).

pivotal_trials.design: Two-part maintenance trial: open-label acute phase (ZS 10 g TID for 48 h), then patients achieving normokalemia randomized double-blind 4:4:4:7 to ZS 5 g, 10 g, or 15 g QD or placebo for 28 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with hyperkalemia (open-label acute phase baseline mean 5.6 mEq/L, range 5.1 to 7.4 mEq/L); 258 patients treated in acute phase.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Randomized withdrawal phase: mean serum potassium value over the period from Day 8 to Day 29, comparing LOKELMA and placebo.
pivotal_trials.n: Maintenance phase randomized: placebo 85, ZS 5 g QD 45, ZS 10 g QD 51, ZS 15 g QD 56.
pivotal_trials.result: All three doses maintained lower mean serum potassium than placebo (Days 8-29 LS mean 4.8, 4.5, 4.4 mEq/L for 5, 10, 15 g vs placebo; p=0.0001 for 5 g, p<0.0001 for 10 g and 15 g).

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction is mild to moderate edema, dose-dependent (4.4% at 5 g, 5.9% at 10 g, 16.1% at 15 g once daily vs 2.4% placebo). In clinical trials 4.1% of patients developed hypokalemia (serum potassium <3.5 mEq/L), which resolved with dose reduction or discontinuation.
target_moa: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate is a non-absorbed zirconium silicate that preferentially captures potassium in exchange for hydrogen and sodium, increasing fecal potassium excretion through binding of potassium in the gastrointestinal lumen, thereby lowering serum potassium.
modality: Small molecule (non-absorbed inorganic zirconium silicate potassium binder).

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held; the application did not raise significant issues regarding safety or effectiveness.

description.text: Added labeling for use in patients on chronic hemodialysis

citations.quote: This supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the labeling for use in patients on chronic hemodialysis.

summary.text: LOKELMA was approved under a traditional (full) approval pathway. The NDA, initially submitted May 26, 2015, received Complete Response Letters (a first CR Letter on May 26, 2016 and a second CR letter dated March 16, 2017) for CMC/facility, clinical pharmacology, and labeling deficiencies; after resubmission on November 22, 2017 the review team agreed the application provided substantial evidence of effectiveness in lowering serum potassium, an accepted surrogate endpoint. No Advisory Committee meeting was held.
